note: REGIME: a narrow AI melt-up inside a rate scare. August payrolls came in at +162k against 55k expected with unemployment steady at 4.1%, which pushed the 2-year to a fresh 52-week high of 4.374% and the 5-year to 4.545% (both new highs), the 10-year to 4.78% and the 30-year to 5.243%, and moved September hike odds back to roughly a coin flip. The broad tape fell on it - S&P 7,718.60 (-0.38%), Dow 53,414.25 (-0.51%), Nasdaq 26,506.99 (-0.29%), with only Tech (+0.44%), Industrials (+0.22%) and Utilities (+0.12%) advancing and Consumer Discretionary (-1.26%), Health Care (-1.04%) and Energy (-0.98%) the worst. But underneath it, AI semis and memory ripped: MU +6.1% to 1,016.59, SNDK +11.9%, SK Hynix +8.14%, ALAB +9.75%, AMD +4.69%. Broadcom's Sep 2 print (revenue $29.6bn +86%, AI semis $16.7bn +221%, FY26 AI guide $58bn, FY27 $115bn, FY28 $230bn) and Dell's record $95.0bn AI-server backlog are the substance behind it. Oil stayed shocked - Brent ~$95.73, +8% on the week, with Hormuz throughput at ~4.9m bpd against 21.6m in Q4 2025, a 77% collapse - yet energy equities fell. Rotation: INTO memory, AI semis and AI hardware; OUT of long-duration software, consumer discretionary and healthcare. Fed Chair Warsh faces a CPI/PPI print next week that decides the September meeting, with Trump publicly demanding cuts. VIX 14.53. spVs200 is an approximation.
